Cache breakpoint.d: A marker (cache_control) in a Claude API request that says 'cache everything up to here'. The next request with an identical beginning reads that part from the cache instead of processing it again.

Cache hit rate.d: The share of input tokens (or requests) served from a prompt cache rather than processed fresh. Higher is cheaper and faster.

Jitter.d: A small random amount added to (or used as) a retry wait, so that many clients that failed at the same moment don't all retry at the same moment.

Token bucket.d: A rate-limiting method: a bucket of allowance refills steadily up to a maximum, and each request spends from it. Short bursts are allowed until the bucket is empty.

Message Batches API.d: Anthropic's asynchronous API for sending many Messages requests at once. Results arrive later (most within an hour, at most 24 hours) at half the normal price.

Spend limit.d: A ceiling on how much an API organisation or workspace may spend in a month. Anthropic sets one per usage tier; you can set your own lower one.

Responses API.d: OpenAI's recommended API for generating text (POST /v1/responses). It replaced Chat Completions as the default for new projects, though Chat Completions is still supported.

Interactions API.d: Google's recommended interface for new Gemini API projects (POST /v1beta/interactions). The older generateContent method is still supported.

Compatibility layer.d: An endpoint that accepts another vendor's request format, such as Claude or Gemini accepting OpenAI SDK calls. Handy for quick comparisons, but usually missing features of the native API.

Vendor lock-in.d: Being tied to one supplier because switching would be costly: your code, prompts, data formats or contracts only fit that supplier.

Ingestion.d: The first stage of a RAG pipeline: collecting documents from their sources (wikis, PDFs, tickets), extracting clean text and metadata, and passing them on for chunking and indexing.

Reciprocal rank fusion.d: A simple way to merge several ranked result lists: each item scores 1/(k + its rank) in every list, and the scores are added. Used to combine keyword and vector search.

Contextual retrieval.d: A RAG technique published by Anthropic in 2024: before indexing, a model writes a short note saying where each chunk sits in its document, and that note is added to the chunk for both embedding and keyword search.

Recall@k.d: A retrieval metric: the share of test questions for which the right chunk appears in the top k results.

Faithfulness.d: Whether every claim in a generated answer is supported by the retrieved sources. An unfaithful answer adds facts the sources do not contain.

Metadata filter.d: A rule applied to stored chunk properties (owner, product, date, permission group) to include or exclude chunks before or during search.
